What Is MEDDICC?

Explainerlowob research

By lowob · 2 September 2026 · 5-minute read · Revenue

MEDDICC is a sales qualification framework for complex B2B deals. The letters stand for Metrics, Economic buyer, Decision criteria, Decision process, Identify pain, Champion and Competition. Each element is a question the seller must answer with evidence from the buyer, not with an opinion. It works best when each letter becomes a field in the CRM and a condition for moving a deal to the next stage.

What MEDDICC means

MEDDICC exists to answer one question: is this a real deal, and will it close when the forecast says? Each letter names a piece of evidence. The definitions below follow those published by MEDDICC, the training firm that maintains the framework.

ElementWhat the seller must establishEvidence that it is true
MetricsThe quantified value the buyer expectsA number the buyer stated, such as hours saved or cost avoided
Economic buyerThe person with overall authority for the decisionA meeting or written confirmation from that person
Decision criteriaThe requirements the buyer will use to judge optionsA written list or RFP requirements
Decision processThe steps the buyer will take to decideNamed steps, owners and dates
Identify painThe business problem driving the purchase, and its costThe buyer's description of consequences if nothing changes
ChampionAn insider with power, influence and credibility who sells for youActions taken, such as arranging a meeting or sharing internal plans
CompetitionAnything competing for the same resources, including doing nothingNamed alternatives, internal builds or a no-decision risk

MEDDICC's own site defines competition broadly, as "anything that competes for the same resources as your solution". That includes an internal project and the option of doing nothing, which often matter more than a rival vendor.

Why it matters for a commercial team

The original problem MEDDICC addressed is still the main one: forecasts built on seller optimism. MEDDICC's published history says the framework was born at PTC in 1996, and credits it with part of PTC's growth to $1 billion in sales within a decade. That claim comes from the framework's own promoters and has not been independently tested.

What has changed is the shape of buying. Forrester found 13 people involved in the average decision and 86% of purchases stalled at some point. With that many stakeholders, the questions about economic buyer, decision process and champion are not formalities. A deal with a keen user and no economic buyer is a conversation, not an opportunity.

Buyers also arrive later. Gartner's 2026 survey found 67% of B2B buyers preferred a rep-free experience, and 45% had used AI during a recent purchase. By the time a seller is involved, decision criteria may already be set. MEDDICC helps a seller find out quickly whether they are shaping the criteria or responding to someone else's.

In lowob's terms, MEDDICC fields are context. An assistant drafting a deal summary, or an agent flagging risk, can only reason about what has been recorded. A blank economic buyer field is a signal in itself.

How to put it into practice

A common failure is a training course and a slide with no change to the CRM. A working version needs three things.

  1. Make each letter a field. Use short structured fields where possible: economic buyer as a contact link, decision process as dated steps, competition as a picklist with free text.
  2. Tie fields to stages. Write exit criteria so that a deal cannot move to proposal without, for example, metrics and a confirmed economic buyer. What Are Pipeline Stage Definitions? covers how to write them.
  3. Inspect in deal reviews. Managers ask for the evidence behind each field, not a score out of seven.
Deal size and complexitySuggested depth
Small, single buyer, short cycleA lighter screen such as BANT may be enough
Mid-market, a few stakeholdersMetrics, economic buyer, pain and champion as required fields
Enterprise, buying group, procurementFull MEDDICC, plus paper process (MEDDPICC)

For a comparison with the older, lighter framework, see What Is BANT, and Is It Still Useful?.

lowob takeaways

  • Evidence, not opinion. Each element needs something the buyer said or did.
  • Fields beat slides. MEDDICC changes forecasts only when it lives in the CRM and the stage rules.
  • Competition includes doing nothing. No-decision is often the strongest alternative in the deal.
  • Match depth to deal size. Full MEDDICC is overhead on a small, single-buyer sale.

Common questions

What does MEDDICC stand for?

Metrics, Economic buyer, Decision criteria, Decision process, Identify pain, Champion and Competition.

What is the difference between MEDDIC, MEDDICC and MEDDPICC?

MEDDIC is the original six elements. MEDDICC adds Competition. MEDDPICC also adds Paper process, the steps from decision to signed contract.

Who created MEDDIC?

It was developed at PTC in 1996. MEDDICC's published history credits Dick Dunkel, working with John McMahon and Jack Napoli.

Is MEDDICC better than BANT?

For complex deals with buying groups, MEDDICC asks for more of the evidence that predicts a close. For small, fast sales, BANT is often sufficient.

Sources and notes

  • MEDDICC, Who Created MEDDIC?, November 2026. Published by the framework's training firm; origin story and growth claims are not independently verified.
  • MEDDICC, MEDDPICC, undated. Training firm's definitions of each element.
  • Forrester, The State Of Business Buying: Companies Still Struggle To Meet Buyer Expectations, December 2024. Analyst survey of more than 16,000 business buyers.
  • Forrester, To Master B2B Buying Mayhem, Providers Must Prioritize Buyers' Needs, December 2024. Press release; source of the 89% and 86% figures.
  • Gartner, Gartner Sales Survey Finds 67% of B2B Buyers Prefer a Rep-Free Experience, March 2026. Survey of 646 B2B buyers.
